39c5a9188796f8f241acd68abb669be6a33d2fab: Regarding the European Parliament plenary meeting's adoption of the "Policy Recommendations on the Changing Geopolitical Situation in East Asia and the Need to Strengthen Cooperation with Like-minded Partners in the Region" report, which recommends that the EU deepens cooperation with democratic partners such as Japan, South Korea and Taiwan, reaffirms the importance of maintaining peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait, and opposes any unilateral change of the status quo through coercion, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs responded as follows:

It is recommended that the EU should deepen cooperation with partners with similar concepts such as Japan, South Korea, Taiwan and ASEAN countries. Taiwan The EU can establish a comprehensive and structural cooperation framework based on operational mechanisms such as the "Trade and Investment Dialogue"; at the same time, it supports Taiwan's meaningful participation in international organizations and technical forums, respects freedom of navigation and overflight in the South China Sea and the Taiwan Strait, and encourages members of the European Parliament and our country's Legislative Yuan to deepen congressional diplomacy. This case once again shows that the European Parliament attaches great importance to peace and stability in Taiwan and the Taiwan Strait. It is also a concrete action to express its firm support for Taiwan after the 2023 "Taiwan-EU Trade and Investment Relations", the 2024 "The People's Republic of China's Improper Interpretation of United Nations General Assembly Resolution 2758 and Continued Military Provocations against Taiwan", and the European Parliament's "Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP) and "Common Security and Defense Policy" (CSDP) 2025 Annual Implementation Report Resolutions. Taiwan will continue to strengthen cooperation with the EU and partners with similar ideas, work together to maintain peace and stability across the Taiwan Strait and the Indo-Pacific region, jointly defend the rules-based international order, and actively make more contributions to global peace, security, and prosperity.
980428c3ec3b5d743ba3045c63a15913faf0a268: Foreign Minister Lin Jialong receives a delegation from the "Transnational Inter-Parliamentary Alliance on China Policy"
a800d20a1e1d49514dff6532a196a0c9401ae9e9: 2026/07/09 Press Release No. 313 Foreign Minister Lin Jialong received an 8-member delegation from the "Inter-Parliamentary Alliance on China Policy" (IPAC) on the afternoon of July 7 this year (2026). In April this year, he issued a statement condemning Beijing for putting its political will above other countries' airspace sovereignty and supporting President Lai Ching-te to communicate freely with international partners without coercion or interference. Minister Lin said that Taiwan will continue to strengthen self-defense and the resilience of society as a whole, and work with IPAC to defend common values ​​such as democracy, freedom, and human rights. Representative Hiccup responded that the visiting delegation members come from different countries and all face challenges brought by authoritarianism. IPAC will firmly support Taiwan's democracy and self-determination rights and firmly believes that only by being fully prepared can real peace be maintained. Political Undersecretary Wu said at the dinner that China continues to expand its authoritarian influence and intrudes on Taiwan with gray zone operations and military intimidation, seriously undermining regional peace and stability. The international community has deeply understood that peace in the Taiwan Strait is inseparable from the interests of all countries, and looks forward to IPAC and partners with similar concepts to continue to deepen cooperation with Taiwan. Former Senator Kaduviti said that the visiting delegation visited Chinese government agencies and civil society organizations and witnessed first-hand the vigorous development of Taiwan's democracy. IPAC will continue to gather transnational members of Congress with similar ideas to jointly defend universal values ​​such as democracy, human rights, and freedom. IPAC was established in June 2020. It is composed of cross-party elected members of parliaments and European Parliaments around the world. Currently, more than 300 members of parliaments and European Parliaments from 44 countries have participated. IPAC is an important transnational parliamentary organization paying attention to the challenges China poses to democratic countries. It is committed to promoting legislation in various countries to prevent China's political and economic penetration and coercion, and has deep international influence. During their stay in Taiwan, in addition to attending the "2026 Taiwan International Ocean Forum" hosted by the Ocean Commission, the delegation jointly met with President Lai Ching-te and Vice President Hsiao Meiqin, received a banquet hosted by National Security Council Secretary-General Joseph Wu and Chairman of the Ocean Commission Kuan Biling, and also visited Black Bear College and Cheng Nanrong Memorial Hall to have in-depth exchanges on topics such as democratic resilience, regional security, and the situation in the Taiwan Strait. 0a356ea13742f850e5966a9a3a9bcc76d7eb4f3d: Wu Zhizhong, Parliamentary Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, hosted the "2026 China Influential Network Annual Conference" welcome dinner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs
4745a47d7f08c71c1fdeddd30f4cbb49d5785099: 2026/07/08 Press Release No. 312 Parliamentary Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Wu Zhizhong hosted the "2026 China in the World Summit" welcome dinner of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs on July 6 today (2026). He interacted with the organizer of the annual conference, Taiwan Democracy Laboratory (Doublethink Lab), and representatives of think tanks, scholars, media and civil society organizations from around the world. The atmosphere was warm. Political Undersecretary Wu said in his speech that the current democratic society is facing challenges brought by the expansion of authoritarianism. In recent years, China has continued to expand its malicious influence through military threats, economic coercion, cyber attacks, disinformation, and transnational suppression. It recently enacted the National Unity and Progress Promotion Law, which has triggered concerns in the international community that it may institutionalize and normalize transnational suppression. Political Secretary Wu pointed out that the "China Influence Network Annual Conference" brings together experts and practitioners in various fields to help deepen understanding and exchanges on Chinese issues, and wished this year's annual conference a complete success. In his speech, Wu Ming-Hsuan, co-founder and CEO of Taiwan Democracy Laboratory, thanked the Ministry of Foreign Affairs for hosting the banquet and the enthusiastic participation of distinguished guests from all over the world. He also said that since its establishment, the "China Influence Network" has successively held annual conferences in Berlin, Germany, Taipei, Taiwan, and Johannesburg, South Africa. This year is the second time it is held in Taiwan. This year’s annual conference attracted more than 300 attendees, planned more than 60 breakout sessions and workshops, and was attended by about 100 domestic and foreign speakers. It is the largest conference in history. We hope that the distinguished guests can use this platform to fully discuss how to respond to the expansion of China’s influence. The "China Influence Network" is a global community launched by the Taiwan Democracy Laboratory in 2019. It aims to bring together civil society, academic institutions, researchers, media and policymakers from all over the world to study China's influence. It releases the "China Influence Index" (China Index) every year to evaluate China's influence and penetration in various countries from nine aspects including law, military, foreign policy, domestic politics, and economy. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs will continue to cooperate with similar-minded civil society groups such as the Taiwan Democracy Laboratory to jointly enhance democratic resilience and safeguard the rules-based international order. (E)

69f764c602f2c116d186ac1f9c45f222f5c48c53: 2026/07/06 Press Release No. 311 U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth (D-IL) will visit Taiwan from July 6 to 8 this year (2026). During her visit to Taiwan, she will meet with President Lai Ching-te and high-level officials of the Chinese government. The two sides will exchange views on important issues such as Taiwan-US relations, regional security, economic, trade and technological cooperation, as well as the situation in the Taiwan Strait and Indo-Pacific region. Foreign Minister Lin Jialong expressed his sincere welcome to Senator Duckworth for his second visit. Senator Duckworth is a member of the "Senate Taiwan Connection" in the U.S. Congress. She has long supported deepening the Taiwan-U.S. partnership. In the past, she not only supported the friendship-Taiwan bill and signed a joint letter of friendship with China many times in the past, she also flew to Taiwan on a U.S. military plane when the COVID-19 epidemic in China was severe and the country was in urgent need of vaccines, announcing that the U.S. government would donate vaccines to Taiwan. This year coincides with the 250th anniversary of the founding of the United States and the 30th anniversary of Taiwan's direct presidential election. Senator Duckworth and bipartisan senators jointly sponsored a resolution recognizing Taiwan's democratic achievements and reaffirming the United States' security commitment to Taiwan based on the Taiwan Relations Act and the "Six Assurances." He also co-sponsored the "STAND with Taiwan Act" (STAND with Taiwan Act) together with Senator Dan Sullivan (R-AK), hoping to use severe sanctions to deter China from invading Taiwan. Foreign Minister Lin Jialong thanked Senator Duckworth for visiting Taiwan again at this important moment, fully demonstrating his firm support for Taiwan. Illinois Treasurer Michael Frerichs and State Senator Paul Faraci will also participate in part of the group's itinerary, looking forward to jointly deepening connections between Taiwan and the United States at the local level. In the face of challenges such as the expansion of authoritarianism, gray zone coercion, and economic coercion, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs will continue to work closely with the U.S. Congress, executive departments, and friends from all walks of life on the basis of the existing good foundation to steadily promote the all-round partnership between Taiwan and the United States in the fields of security, economy, trade, and science and technology, and jointly create regional peace, stability, and prosperity. (E)

980902a5405393df3dbdf09ccadacef89ddd597f: Regarding China’s test-launch of strategic missiles into the Pacific on July 6, which disregards the importance of regional peace and stability, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs responded as follows:

China should exercise rational restraint and avoid taking any actions that may increase the risk of miscalculation or endanger regional security. e62306bc3f8400af28f23609c583d8a7f8c6e01e: Parliamentary Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Chen Ming-chi attended the "Global Brainstorming Forum" and encouraged young students from National Taiwan University to create Taiwan's value
160bb3da9fdf4a4e446b0dbc2b31cc611672aea4: 2026/07/03 News Reference No. 054 Parliamentary Secretary of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs Chen Mingqi attended the closing ceremony of the 17th "Global Initiatives Symposium, GIS Taiwan 2026" organized by National Taiwan University on July 3 this year (2026), and delivered the speech "Bond and Beyond: Building Trust in a Divided World" (Bond and Beyond: Building Trust in a Divided World) World), he encouraged many young students at home and abroad to build a cross-border network of trust and cooperation in an international environment full of uncertainties, and jointly build a more resilient future for Taiwan. In his speech, Vice-Chancellor Chen echoed the theme of this forum "Bond and Beyond" and said that what is lacking in today's world is not connections, but "partnerships" that can withstand the test of crises, pressures and challenges; future international cooperation should not only pursue efficiency, but should also be based on trust, resilience and shared responsibility. Vice-Chang Chen pointed out that globalization has not ended but has entered a new stage of development. How to build a resilient cooperation network has become an important issue faced by all countries. When talking about Taiwan's role, Chen said that the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has actively promoted the concept of "comprehensive diplomacy" proposed by Minister Lin Jialong in recent years, combining democratic values, partnerships with similar concepts, and Taiwan's technological and industrial advantages to deepen international cooperation, making Taiwan not only an important link in the global supply chain, but also a trustworthy, capable and willing international partner willing to share responsibilities. Taiwan is willing to continue to combine its advantages in technology, talent, industry, and democratic systems to share experience and deepen cooperation with the international community to jointly respond to global challenges. Chen encouraged all young people participating in the forum to cherish the interpersonal connections established during the forum. Regardless of whether they invest in business, government, academic research, or civil society in the future, they should continue to cultivate the ability to cooperate and build trust across cultures, so that they can work together to overcome challenges and create greater value. The "Global Brainstorming Forum" was founded in 2008 and is independently organized by the student team of National Taiwan University. Over the years, it has invited young people from all over the world to gather in Taiwan to exchange and dialogue on important global issues. It is the largest international student academic forum in Taiwan, demonstrating the energy of Taiwanese youth to participate in global public affairs and promote public diplomacy. (E)

ca6f42df56a1c6fd09dac92b528498b4e226f1f4: The Chinese government will establish an "Office in Phoenix" in Arizona, USA, to further deepen exchanges and cooperation between Taiwan and the United States.

6a59b443f640fd0e4a8511ffff858ef589e5c0b6: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs revised the subsidy measures for investment in friendly countries, expanded support for Taiwanese businessmen, and deepened the economic diplomacy of the "Rongbang Plan"
086228c76864bc846784a7f99c95b84699ec1c91: 2026/07/03 Press Release No. 306 In order to accelerate the promotion of the "Rongbang Plan", deepen economic and trade cooperation between my country and friendly countries, and encourage Chinese enterprises to invest in friendly countries, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs has revised the "Measures for Encouraging Enterprises to Invest in Countries with Diplomatic Relations" and will be promulgated and implemented on July 1 this year (2026). This revision of the law reduces the initial costs and investment risks for enterprises to enter emerging markets by relaxing subsidy projects, increasing subsidy amounts, and strengthening support for inspections in friendly countries. It encourages China's advantageous industries and the government to work together to develop in friendly countries, assist friendly countries to enhance industrial energy, expand international markets, further strengthen bilateral economic and trade cooperation, and implement the goal of mutual benefit and common prosperity. In order to implement the policy direction of "Comprehensive Diplomacy" and "Prosperity Plan", this amendment further strengthens the institutional support for enterprises to invest in friendly countries, hoping to attract more Taiwanese enterprises to invest in the friendly countries' markets, and combine China's advantageous industries such as smart agriculture, food processing, smart medical care, green energy, information communications, smart transportation and sustainable tourism with the development needs of the friendly countries to promote local investment and long-term operations, and transform Taiwan's industrial strength into an important force that deepens friendship and promotes the sustainable development of friendly countries. The key points of this revision are as follows: 1. Relax the scope of application of subsidy projects: Based on the actual investment needs of enterprises, the scope of application of subsidy projects will be expanded to include local employee salaries, factory equipment, business premises or land rent and financing interest, etc., and the original restriction of selecting one application will be removed to improve the flexibility and practicality of subsidy measures. 2. Increase the cumulative maximum subsidy amount: Considering that prices, labor costs and initial capital costs of enterprises’ overseas investments have continued to rise in recent years, the cumulative maximum subsidy amount for enterprises within 7 years will be increased from the original NT$20 million to NT$60 million to provide enterprises with more substantial and effective investment support. 3. Increase the subsidy for investment inspections in friendly countries: In response to the increase in international air tickets and transportation costs, the upper limit of air ticket subsidies for companies to go to diplomatic countries to inspect the investment environment, evaluate market conditions and negotiate cooperation opportunities will be increased to NT$100,000 to encourage businesses to actively evaluate their investment plans in friendly countries. In the face of global supply chain reorganization and industrial layout adjustment, AIA is not only an important diplomatic partner of Taiwan, but also has high potential for industrial cooperation, market expansion and regional layout. By amending the law, the policy support will be greatly enhanced, hoping to reduce the initial risks of enterprises' overseas investment layout, encourage more Taiwanese businessmen to invest and set up factories in friendly countries, establish supply chain nodes, and expand markets. It will also help friendly countries improve industrial technology, create local jobs and promote economic development, forming a win-win cooperation. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs emphasized that the core spirit of the "Rongbang Plan" is to gradually upgrade the traditional one-way assistance model to a partnership with investment, trade, industrial cooperation and common development as the core, and promote a new model of "allied countries and common prosperity". In the future, we will continue to combine the resources of China's diplomatic missions abroad, CCICED and relevant ministries and committees to assist Taiwanese businessmen to expand the markets of friendly countries, promote the industrial upgrading of friendly countries, expand exports and create jobs, so that Taiwanese enterprises can become important partners in deepening friendship and promoting common prosperity. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs will continue to promote the "comprehensive diplomacy" policy, closely integrate my country's advantageous industries and civil society, deepen economic and trade cooperation with friendly countries through public-private collaboration, deepen bilateral friendship with substantial economic and trade momentum, assist Taiwanese businessmen to steadily deepen their global presence, and work with friendly countries to achieve a mutually beneficial and co-prosperous partnership. c9b249e0f2a7d2d08bc7b10a709d662316710455: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs solemnly opposes China's implementation of the so-called "National Unity and Progress Promotion Law" to carry out long-arm jurisdiction and transnational suppression, and calls on the international community to jointly counter the expansion of authoritarianism
12ae7057dedc51c0ea970ed5f15dc9e1d6671038: 2026/07/01 Press Release No. 303 In response to the Chinese government's implementation of the so-called "National Unity and Progress Promotion Law" on July 1 this year (2026), in an attempt to use its domestic laws and regulations to carry out long-arm jurisdiction and transnational suppression, expand threats and intimidation to the people of our country and other countries, and seriously infringe the sovereignty of various countries and international human rights, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs expresses strong condemnation and solemn opposition to this. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs pointed out that the above-mentioned law, in the form of domestic law, clearly imposes jurisdiction over organizations and individuals outside China. It serves as the legal basis for China’s expansion of long-arm jurisdiction and transnational suppression, and poses a considerable threat to global freedom, democracy, and human rights. In the future, if people from various countries have relevant words and deeds that are not acceptable to China, they may be targeted or pursued under this law. The international community should jointly condemn China's once again authoritarian expansion of its domestic laws. In addition, many provisions of the law are based on China's so-called "undermining of ethnic unity," "creating ethnic divisions," and "unfavorable to ethnic unity and progress," and other concepts that lack clear definitions. They give China's law enforcement agencies room for arbitrary interpretation, making it difficult for the public to identify risks and thus conduct self-censorship, creating a chilling effect and seriously violating the principles of legal clarity and proportionality that should be valued in a country governed by the rule of law. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs reiterated that Taiwan, the Republic of China, is a sovereign and independent country and is not affiliated with the People's Republic of China. None of China's domestic laws are binding on Taiwan, and it has no power to criminalize Taiwanese people. As a democratic and free country, Taiwan's people enjoy freedom of speech and thought in accordance with the law, and China does not tolerate interference or interference. The Ministry of Foreign Affairs emphasized that when authoritarianism exports fear, democratic countries must improve social resilience; when authoritarian forces try to create divisions, partners with similar ideals should deepen cooperation to jointly respond. As an important member of the democratic camp, Taiwan will continue to strengthen its social resilience through international cooperation and resist the Chinese government's transnational suppression. (E)

1d21d694f2526a6ba673f840165ff21cf53dc1ae: Chen Ming-chi Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Republic of China (Taiwan) September 22, 2025 (As Prepared for Delivery) President Tseng Yung-chuan of the ROC Chapter of the WLFD; The Honorable Dennis Rogan, Deputy Speaker of the UK House of Lords; The Honorable Diarmuid Wilson, member of the Irish Senate; The Honorable Tina Rose Muña Barnes, Senator of the Guam Legislature; The Honorable Bruce Knotts, President and CEO of the NGO Committee on Disarmament, Peace, and Security; Excellencies Ambassadors and Honorable Representatives; Distinguished participants; Ladies and gentlemen: Good morning! On behalf of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, I would like to extend a warm welcome to our dear friends from around the world attending today’s event. It is a great privilege to be invited to speak here today. I am delighted to witness the outstanding achievements of the WLFD and its strong dedication to upholding our shared beliefs. The world is facing more daunting challenges than ever. Authoritarianism and collusion among autocratic regimes have been spreading, thereby eroding our values and the rules-based international order. This development has further divided free and open societies and disrupted global peace and prosperity. These challenges may be political, military, economic, social, or even hybrid in nature. They threaten to undermine our defense mechanisms. External forces frequently enlist the aid of local collaborators who engage in influence operations and disinformation campaigns so as to generate turmoil and distrust within our societies. All of us must remain highly vigilant in response to such efforts. Taiwan has long stood on the front line defending freedom and democracy from authoritarian expansionism. Over the years, it has had to defend against attacks on its sovereignty and economy and respond to the denial of its fundamental right to participate in international initiatives. Nevertheless, Taiwan has continued to serve as a beacon of freedom, democracy, and resilience, earning respect worldwide. Taiwan is a responsible member of the international community and plays a pivotal role in global supply chains. It remains committed to working with like-minded partners such as the WLFD in safeguarding shared values and protecting common interests. Indeed, Taiwan has been and will continue to be a force for good, advancing pragmatic cooperation and value-added diplomacy to ensure a prosperous and sustainable future for everyone. Taiwan needs the world, and Taiwan matters to the world. This is not a political statement but rather a reflection of reality. In recent years, Taiwan has become an important hub for international nongovernmental organizations (INGOs) that promote democracy and human rights in Asia. Many INGOs have opened offices in Taiwan to further their reach. These include Freedom House, the Westminster Foundation for Democracy, the National Democratic Institute, the International Republican Institute, and the Friedrich Naumann Foundation for Freedom. We look forward to welcoming even more INGOs setting up operations here in the future, as they truly are the catalyst for promoting world peace. In closing, your presence underscores our democratic unity. We must continue to work in solidarity to make the world a better place for future generations. Taiwan is proud to lead the league of freedom and democracy, uphold the principles of liberty and inclusiveness, and promote prosperity and peace for all. I wish you all a pleasant and productive stay, and this conference every success. Thank you.
1daa66d9530839f02f204edb24acc785dc9dbe47: François Chihchung Wu Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs Republic of China (Taiwan) August 5, 2025 (As Prepared for Delivery) Distinguished guests; Ladies and gentlemen: Bonjour, good afternoon! It is a great privilege to introduce our keynote speaker for this afternoon’s session, the Honorable François de Rugy. He is an exceptional leader, a dedicated advocate for Taiwan–France relations, and a personal friend, un ami auquel je tiens beaucoup! During my six years serving as Taiwan’s Ambassador to France, I had the honor of witnessing first-hand François’s outstanding leadership and his unwavering support for democratic values. As Minister d’Etat, Minister of State, number 2 in the French government, he received then–Minister Gong Mingxin of Taiwan’s National Development Council — the first time a French Minister of State welcomed a Taiwanese ministerial-level official in his ministry — a gesture that spoke volumes about his friendship and support for democratic Taiwan. François has also served as President of the National Assembly and multiple terms as a member of parliament, these experiences have made him a strong and respected voice for reform and progress, not only in France, but also around the world -- and very much here in Taiwan! As a friend of Taiwan, François has played a vital role in strengthening the partnership between our two nations. He first visited Taiwan in 2016 during his tenure as Vice President of the National Assembly, marking the beginning of a deep and lasting engagement. In 2020, he became Chairman of the National Assembly’s France–Taiwan Parliamentary Friendship Group, working tirelessly to foster closer relations. Thanks to his leadership, in 2021 the French National Assembly overwhelmingly passed its first-ever resolution supporting Taiwan’s participation in international organizations. Later that year, François returned to Taiwan to further solidify our ties. Today, François will draw on years of experience to analyze the current geopolitical landscape and explore strategies to address global challenges. I am confident that His insights will help us navigate the complexities ahead and advance our shared vision. And now, please join me in giving a warm welcome to the Honorable François de Rugy — a true friend of Team Taiwan and Team Freedom. François, sachez que ton amitié compte beaucoup pour nous. Merci!

ad6e24e30b2a253b9ef9bbc77e3f2ae658597b52: Dr. Lin Chia-lung Minister of Foreign Affairs Republic of China (Taiwan) April 24, 2025 (As Prepared for Delivery) Ladies and gentlemen: Good morning! The opening of the 5G Government Network and Smart City Development Project operations center is a milestone in Eswatini’s national development. It is an honor to be jointly hosting this ceremony with Prime Minister Dlamini (Lamini). We are witnessing an important step toward achieving His Majesty King Mswati (m-swa-ti)’s vision of making Eswatini a first-world nation. ICT is developing at a rapid pace. Digital and smart technologies are improving the quality of life, driving social progress, and creating economic growth. They have become a part of our everyday lives. Taiwan is known as a smart technology island. We have worked hard to develop reliable networks, reinforce digital governance, safeguard digital sovereignty, and build smart cities. In these areas, we have achieved some success and improved the well-being of our people. As an active and responsible member of the international community, Taiwan is keen to share its achievements with allied nations. During his tenure as CEO of the National Disaster Management Agency in 2022, Prime Minister Dlamini took part in Taiwan’s Advanced Training Program on Disaster Prevention Technology and Management. Last month, Mayor Mkhonta (m-kon-ta) and CEO Fakudze (fa-ku-ze) attended the Smart City Expo in Taiwan, where they had the opportunity to see developments and applications of smart city initiatives. Taiwan and Eswatini are working closely together on the 5G Government Network and Smart City Development Project. This initiative will support economic and social development in Eswatini. It will create a dedicated 5G network for the government to ensure digital sovereignty and maintain network security. Transportation, public safety, and disaster prevention systems will be connected with 5G infrastructure. This will transform Mbabane into a smart city. The program will also increase the efficiency of urban governance. The capital city of Mbabane is the starting point. Moving forward, the project will be expanded to other major cities. Eswatini is on a path to becoming a 5G nation with first-world status. This project shows that Taiwan can help. It also demonstrates that Taiwan-plus-Eswatini cooperation is greater than the sum of its parts. Guided by the spirit of Nkwe, Taiwan will continue to collaborate with Eswatini. We plan to introduce digital and smart technologies into other sectors such as health care and business. Our goal is to create a technological Taiwan and a smart Eswatini. Let us keep working together to improve the well-being of our people. Thank you.
4471ed53913548ab900c984cf499b8fa1bc467d8: Dr. Lin Chia-lung Minister of Foreign Affairs Republic of China (Taiwan) February 24, 2025 (As delivered) Ladies and gentlemen: Good afternoon! It is a great pleasure to attend the 2025 MOFA Taiwan Fellowship Lunar New Year reception. On behalf of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MOFA), I want to extend my warmest welcome to all of the distinguished Taiwan Fellowship scholars. I would also like to express my sincere appreciation to Director General Wang and her capable staff for organizing today’s event. Without your hard work, today’s event would not have been possible. MOFA established the Taiwan Fellowship in 2010. This program aims to attract exceptional scholars and experts from around the world to come to Taiwan and conduct research related to our country, cross-strait relations, and the Indo-Pacific region. To date, over 1,500 scholars have benefited from this program. Since assuming the post of foreign minister, I have increased the number of recipients from 100 to 125, demonstrating MOFA’s strong commitment to the program. This year, we are pleased to welcome scholars from 41 countries. Academics conducting research here not only serve as important ambassadors between Taiwan and their home countries but also link our country to the rest of the world. You all play a vital role in influencing how people see Taiwan by sharing your experiences here with people back home or on various platforms such as articles or social media. We encourage all of you to share stories of your time in Taiwan, speak up for our country, and help the world gain a better understanding of Taiwan. MOFA is currently implementing integrated diplomacy policy and the Diplomatic Allies Prosperity Project. Academic communities and people-to-people networks are important pillars of our efforts. Knowledge sharing is critical for a country’s national development. I therefore look forward to exchanging ideas with all of you. This year, we celebrate the Year of the Snake. The snake is a creature that represents intelligence, flexibility, and dynamic energy. My wife and I wrote a spring couplet, which translates as “deftly reaching far, smoothly realizing This conveys our expectations for the new year. By being as flexible and wise as a serpent, we can surely overcome all challenges. Today’s reception provides you the chance to connect with other fellowship recipients, domestic scholars, the ambassadors or representatives of your home countries, and the administrative staff of everyone in this program. of the Snake. Happy New Year! Thank you.

In this 26th year of diplomatic relation, we are bound to have more and closer cooperation, and address regional and global challenges together. Finally, I sincerely thank every friend for attending the dinner tonight. I wish everyone continued health and success. Thank you! Mesulang!

a7d413dda2173a24a87c034e58d767e2fe193fce: The 30-year-old TaiwanICDF leverages technology to give other nations the means to achieve food security. Taiwan is committed to facilitating the agricultural development of its allies and other like-minded countries, an aspiration underscored last November at the third edition of the Development Focus Forum in Taipei City. Organized by the government-supported Taiwan International Cooperation and Development Fund (TaiwanICDF), the event has taken place every three months since May 2025, with the latest iteration centering on smart agriculture. Taiwanese and international experts gathered for the event with a focus on overseas projects implemented by the fund. Speakers and panelists shared how smart agriculture can reshape the the, and TaiwanICDF explained how its Taiwan Technical Missions (TTM) use smart solutions to facilitate transformation in agriculture abroad. Deputy Secretary General Hsieh Pei-fen (谢 Pei-fen) said the forum offers diverse perspectives that provide new focal points for future TaiwanICDF international aid projects sector. Taiwan has a long history of providing agricultural assistance overseas, in areas spanning crop production, pig farming and aquaculture. In 1959 the government sent a group of 11 agricultural specialists to South Vietnam, marking the beginning of the nation’s overseas aid in food production. In 1961 Taiwan launched Operation Vanguard, a project that sent an agricultural technical mission to Liberia. The endeavor, the first of its kind in Africa, was a success and subsequently replicated in 10 other countries on the continent over the next three years. The first such mission from Taiwan to Latin America arrived in the Dominican Republic in 1964. Founded in 1996, TaiwanICDF is the nation’s foremost foreign aid organization offering assistance in various areas including agriculture. Projects implemented by the fund send specialists to partner nations, offer training sessions in Taiwan and carry out lending and investment plans. To date Taiwan has helped over 80 countries further develop their agriculture, and currently TaiwanICDF has TTMs on the ground in 21 countries including Saudi Arabia, Tanzania and Thailand. The organization’s statistics from 2022 indicated that its agricultural projects created 15,000 jobs that year. Food Security The main goal of TaiwanICDF’s current agricultural work is to ensure food security and meet basic human needs in partner countries in line with the United Nations’ Sustainable Development Goal 2, which aims to end hunger and improve nutrition. In Caribbean ally Haiti, where rice is a staple food, various production enhancement projects, such as training Haitian technical staff in Taiwan, applying effective irrigation system maintenance and, most importantly, producing high-quality, high-yield rice strains, have been implemented across the nation over the past 12 years. Statistics show that farms with TTM input produced more than 2,100 tons of resilient seed rice harvested across 618 hectares of paddies last year. TaiwanICDF works with European Union funding and the Tuvalu government to undertake agricultural projects in the nation. 88c54ed5de33a88d082cc464c3a525b2a4c2351d: Taiwan’s mountainous national parks are home to endangered endemic wildlife species like the Formosan landlocked salmon and Swinhoe’s pheasant. The NPS is also responsible for Shoushan National Nature Park in Kaohsiung City, as well as sites covered by the Wetland Conservation Act of 2013 and Coastal Zone Management Act of 2015. Yushan National Park, named for the country’s highest mountain contained within its borders, is the largest of the assets. Yushan, Shei-Pa and Taroko contain nearly 60 percent of Taiwan’s peaks over 3,000 meters. Each year around 250,000 visitors apply for permits to access protected areas of the three parks, demonstrating the strong appeal of rugged mountains and sweeping views. In 2025 the NPS expanded a centralized mountain permit mobile app featuring emergency signal broadcasting, offline maps and real-time condition updates from Shei-Pa to include both Yushan and Taroko national parks. 884b5621fbafbe815a10c3d398fc7616e43ed145: Hengchun Tropical Botanical Garden is a living archive of endemic and rare flora. In Taiwan’s tropical south, climate and weather patterns affect heat, leaving high temperatures with soft breezes and sudden rain. Ocean currents from the Pacific and South China Sea converge offshore and create storms that sweep across the land, shaping a unique ecosystem full of specialized climate-adapted plants and shrubs. Climatically and biologically, Hengchun Peninsula stands apart. South of the Tropic of Cancer, it is Taiwan Island’s only region with year-round tropical warmth and pronounced wet and dry seasons. Its flora is distinct from Taiwan’s subtropical regions, having evolved in isolation amid limestone geology and strong monsoon winds. “More than a thousand plant species have been recorded here, including over 200 rare taxa,” said Huang Chun-yuan, director of Hengchun Research Center. For plants dispersed from across oceans, the peninsula often serves as a first landfall. Hengchun Tropical Botanical Garden is located at the southernmost tip of Taiwan, between the Pacific Ocean, Bashi Channel and Taiwan Strait. (Courtesy of FANCA, Pingtung Branch) The center administers Hengchun Tropical Botanical Garden, a facility that covers nearly 64 hectares of uplifted coral limestone. The garden dates to the early 20th century, when Japanese botanist Antei Tashiro laid the foundations of tropical plant research in Taiwan with a 1901 proposal to establish a site on Hengchun Peninsula for tropical plant experimentation. The Hengchun Tropical Plant Cultivation Farm was formally established the next year under the Bureau of Productive Industries, and offices, dormitories and nurseries were added in 1907. Forestry Research Institute, Hengchun Branch Director Wang Jen-li, second right, and former Taiwan Provincial Assembly Speaker, Huang Chao-chin, third right, pose in the 1950s outside the precursor to today’s Hengchun Tropical Botanical Garden and Research Center. (Courtesy of Taiwan Forestry Research Institute) An undated image of a map of the Hengchun Tropical Arboretum (Courtesy of TFRI) The site was formally designated the Tropical Useful Plant Specimen Garden in 1908 and undertook to gather useful tropical plants from around the world to see which might be productively developed in Taiwan. The garden received its current name in 1945 and was incorporated into what is now Kenting National Forest Recreation Area in 1968 to combine research with recreation. Land ownership and plant management remain with the facility’s administrator, Taiwan Forestry Research Institute, while visitor services, exhibitions, environmental maintenance and ticketing are handled by the local branch of the Forestry and Nature Conservation Agency. A protected fern species, Diplazium sinense, in Hengchun Tropical Botanical Garden highlights the site’s role in conserving rare and endemic tropical flora in southern Taiwan. (Photo by Krakias Kai) Record and Research Adjacent to Sheding Nature Park within Kenting National Park, the garden forms part of a larger ecological continuum shaped by monsoons and long-term isolation. “What distinguishes the garden today is its role as a living archive,” said Huang. The germplasm bank is organized into 17 thematic zones, some defined by human history, such as the Ethno-plant Collection, which documents species historically used in Indigenous medicine and the Crafting of useful goods. Others follow geography, including regional collections for Orchid Island and Green Island, safeguarding small, isolated populations vulnerable to typhoons and other natural threats. Additional zones focus on plants endemic to Hengchun Peninsula, aquatic plants and specialized groups such as crotons and ferns. Together, these collections act as a biological bulwark against an uncertain future by preserving species whose natural habitats are increasingly constrained. Each year seeds from approximately 100 species are collected and documented, forming the basis of the garden’s research collections and germplasm bank. This is a normal day for search and rescue dogs, which are trained and assessed by the International Search and Rescue Dog Organization (IRO). In rural districts such as Xinshe in Taichung City, travelers can wake to quiet neighborhoods, locally sourced breakfasts and hosts who treat hospitality as part of daily life. These settings capture the appeal of vacation properties that bear the Taiwan Host mark, which offer an alternative to conventional hotels. In 2023 there were around 1,587 such properties operating, out of over 10,717 registered bed-and-breakfasts. As the sector continues to expand, industry groups and government agencies have worked to establish standards that support quality, safety and sustainable growth. Shaped by personal vision and regional identity, Taiwan Host locations are a distinctive part of Taiwan’s tourism landscape. Many utilize farming or historical properties that emphasize a connection to local industry or history. For example, the living room of the Xinshe homestay owned by Lai Shuw-wei, chair of the Taiwan Rural Accommodation Association (TRAA), features a photo wall displaying images taken in the 1960s by her parents-in-law, forming an extensive archive introducing guests to local stories. The photographs are rotated regularly, allowing the narrative to evolve over time, while the location, surrounded by mushroom farms, vineyards and apple orchards, further embeds the guest experience within the surrounding agricultural landscape. “As interest in this type of accommodation grew, so did the need for clear standards and sustainable practices,” Lai said. Behind the welcome framework lies a of guidelines, industry coordination and individual commitment that defines the sector and strengthens the role of homestays in the domestic tourism landscape. Properties must meet minimum scores across categories such as space, environment, service and sustainability, as well as fully comply with essential requirements including fire safety and insurance coverage. Guest rooms, bathrooms and emergency preparedness protocols are all verified in on-site inspections. Further training centers on online marketing, experience-driven promotion, brand identity and distinctive experience design, reinforcing the idea that hosting is a professional skill that evolves over time. 22addd3408c55a71d154d9eca55c0d61e701464e: Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim, left, attends the opening ceremony of 2025 Baosheng Cultural Festival hosted by Dalongdong Baoan Temple in Taipei. (Courtesy of Presidential Office) Taiwan’s traditional religious festivities are immersive experiences that continue to evolve with contemporary society. In April 2025 Dalongdong Baoan Temple in Taipei City’s Datong District hosted its annual Baosheng Cultural Festival to mark the birthday of Baosheng Dadi, the god of medicine, on the 15th day of the third lunar month. At the opening ceremony, Vice President Hsiao Bi-khim praised the UNESCO-recognized restoration of the temple, which was originally built in the early 19th century, and highlighted the event’s enduring spiritual meaning and social value. “With its blend of folk belief, cultural customs and tourism appeal, the festival offers great warmth to Taipei residents and enhances Taiwan’s international visibility,” she said. Now more than three decades old, the celebration features fireworks and roaming performers that draw visitors from home and abroad, turning a historic religious observance into a vibrant spectacle. Japanese organizers of the Kenkayama festival at Fushiki Shrine in Toyama prefecture contribute towering lantern floats to Qingshan’s parade. (Photo by Chen Mei-ling) Baoan Temple’s approach reflects the enduring popularity of urban religious festivals, also seen at Monga Qingshan Temple on Wanhua District’s Guiyang Street, Taipei’s oldest commercial thoroughfare. Last year marked the temple’s 170th anniversary, which coincided with the annual celebration of its main deity Qingshan Wang’s birthday in the 10th lunar month. Co-hosted with local agencies, the latest edition included art exhibitions, guided tours, pop concerts and televised variety shows. International exchange also played a role, with organizers of the Kenkayama festival at Fushiki Shrine in Japan’s Toyama prefecture bringing towering lantern floats to join Qingshan’s nighttime parade. Lin Mao-hsien, an associate professor in the Department of Taiwanese Languages and Literature at National Taichung University of Education, said that such creative programming, arranged in collaboration with the Taipei City Government’s Department of Information and Tourism and the state-backed General Association of Chinese Culture, adds new momentum to Qingshan’s celebrations. Keelung City’s Waimushan Xie’an Temple holds a marine pilgrimage honoring Wang Ye and Mazu along Taiwan’s north coast. (Courtesy of Tourism Administration) See Devotion With temples dedicated to a wide array of deities spread across urban neighborhoods and rural communities alike, there is no lack of festivals in the calendar. The third lunar month is especially rich in large-scale events, led by weekslong pilgrimages honoring Mazu, the beloved sea goddess worshiped at more than 1,000 temples nationwide. Her birthday on the 23rd day of the lunar month draws vast crowds onto the roads. Signature events such as the Taichung Mazu International Festival organized by Dajia Jenn Lann Temple in Taichung City, along with pilgrimages associated with Miaoli County’s Baishatun Gongtian Temple, are officially recognized as part of Taiwan’s intangible cultural heritage by the Ministry of Culture. Among the country’s 24 designated major folk traditions, several Mazu-related events have been selected by the Ministry of Transportation and Communications’ Tourism Administration (TA) for focused international promotion in 2026 and 2027. Upgraded from a bureau in 2023, the TA spotlights Taiwan’s folk cultures by hosting international media visits and launching campaigns that engage social media influencers and public figures. According to the agency, Taiwan’s religious festivals usually offer distinctive, immersive experiences marked by movement, color and collective participation, qualities that give the country its unique character in the global tourism landscape. Lin noted that while many destinations compete through historic sites or natural sites scenery, Taiwan’s living cultural activities like temple festivals and Mazuages appeal to both domestic and overseas visitors. The autumn ceremony welcoming Wang Ye at Donggang Donglong Temple in Pingtung County culminates in the burning of a large boat on the beach. (Photo by Jimmy Lin) A Mazu palanquin from Baishatun Gongtian Temple in Miaoli County shakes as it receives divine cues guiding the procession’s path. (Courtesy of TA) Lin personally joins these events every year, and pilgrim students enrolled in his courses on the culture of Taiwan are encouraged to take part. Participation, he emphasized, is cultural rather than doctrine. Students attend to observe folk customs firsthand and experience the trust and emotional connection shared among participants and local residents, who routinely help one another with food, lodging

6349943831a96bf8ddac04444addd2f4c035509b: Smart systems are combating climate change to enhance agricultural productivity. The Ministry of Agriculture (MOA) has made smart agriculture a cornerstone of development since 2017 with a forward-looking policy framework centered on efficient production and digital services. The ministry leverages big data to address demographic challenges faced by small- and medium-sized farms. The resulting proactive, integrated agricultural platforms benefit all stakeholders and strengthen consumer confidence in food safety. Lee Hung-hsi, director of the MOA’s Department of Agricultural Science and Technology, said that the strategic framework emphasizes smart, resilient, sustainable and trustworthy action in conjunction with digital services and artificial intelligence (AI) applications to reduce operational risk and ensure stable production and marketing systems. “Our department coordinates policy planning, technology development and demonstration programs. We also work closely with the Department of Information Technology, Department of Government Ethics and industry authorities such as the Department of Animal Industry, Agriculture and Food Agency, and Fisheries Agency to align with national policies,” Lee said. Drone technology is not weather dependent and can undertake tasks such as crop spraying no matter the conditions, increasing agricultural production efficiency. (Photo Courtesy of Chiayi County Government) The department advances efficiency through four initiatives: smart agriculture, cloud-based digital transformation, chip development and the Internet of Things (IoT). These inform research and innovation, infrastructure, training and growth. Local partnerships and subsidies from the central government resulted in 194 technology transfers, 88 registered service providers in the smart agriculture tech system, eight startups and 480 smart agriculture sites across 4,000 locations. Research outcomes have been integrated into 13 technologies for floriculture, rice, vegetables, aquaculture and the raising of poultry, all accessible via a portal for consultation and matchmaking. The MOA also supports over 20 expert system platforms for data applications, publicly available on the website to foster government transparency and enable service providers and research institutions to leverage data for commercial use or collaborative development. As an example, the MOA launched a project last year to collect agricultural pest and disease images to improve diagnostic accuracy of AI analysis systems. Chen Wen-hui shows off papaya at a plantation where he uses data collected by sensors to fine-tune irrigation, among other tasks. (Photo by Chen Wen-hui) Smart Thinking Chiayi County’s smart agriculture policy was launched in 2018 with funding from the Ministry of Economic Affairs and is now fully financed by the county government. With training, subsidies and equipment leasing programs, it ensures that technology reaches sites rather than staying in laboratories, rendering precision agriculture both practical and attainable. Papaya and pineapple plantations demonstrate how nutrient data platforms optimize irrigation, balance and pest control strategies, automating management for higher yields. In Shuishang Township, papaya grower Chen Wen-hui (陈文伟) connected his 12-hectare operation to digital monitoring and precision management systems. The fully integrated system featuring micro-mist cooling, smart fertigation drips and a field microclimate network resulted in labor requirements dropping by 40 percent, nearly 30 percent decrease in energy use and yields rising by around 20 percent. This gained the operation a Traceable Agricultural Product (TAP) certification, and by 2023 it achieved the Taiwan Good Agricultural Product PLUS standard, which covers four key areas: good agricultural practices, food safety, labor safety and environmental sustainability, as well as integrated crop and pest management. The success was recognized by the MOA and subsequently Japan, where this precision-farming model has been replicated in Chiba prefecture and on Ishigaki Island using Taiwan-made equipment and systems. Pineapples are larger and sweeter as a result of precision soil and fertilizer management. (Courtesy of A-Mei Pineapple) In Minxiong Township, third-generation pineapple grower Chen Ying-yen (陈英覿) uses AI-assisted fertilization models and real-time monitoring to produce fruit that has a longer shelf life and better flavor. On site, Taiwan’s first ride-on dual-row cultivator and fertilizer applicator is linked to digital controls for weeding, fertilization and soil management. Chen leverages the sixth sector industrialization model of primary agriculture, secondary processing and tertiary marketing and retail through his A-Mei Pineapple brand and the Wang Lai Shan Pineapple Cultural Park. 15a376d6e31422c32cdde2f80d78eef647ecdae3: Pangolin populations in Taiwan are rebounding. In early October 2025 joy erupted at the Kaohsiung City Matoushan Nature and Humanity Association (KCMNHA) when National Pingtung University of Science and Technology (NPUST) confirmed the pregnancies of two pangolins, A-hua and Hsiao-chi. “We were ecstatic at the news, especially because it reflects a healthy ecosystem at Matoushan,” said KCMNHA President Huang Hui-min (Huimin Huang). Founded in 2019, the association grew out of a successful grassroots campaign led by Huang to stop the construction of a landfill that would have threatened local wildlife. Today the nongovernmental organization protects native species by tracking them with transmitters and researching their behavior in the wild. It also runs outreach programs that introduce residents to the area’s diverse flora and fauna, helping build a sense of stewardship toward animals such as pangolins. These elusive mammals roam the region’s forested foothills, typically at altitudes below 1,000 meters. Locals are encouraged to report sightings and alert the group to any activity that might endanger them. While pangolins are now a treasured species in Taiwan, decades ago they faced serious threats. From the 1950s to 1970s they were hunted for their skin, which was processed into leather for export. Conditions began to improve in the 1980s, but pangolins continued to be captured for their meat and scales, long believed to offer health benefits. Real protection came with 1989’s Act on Wildlife Conservation that strictly prohibited, killing or trading of protected species. Kaohsiung City Matoushan Nature and Humanity Association members search for transmitter signals. (Photo by Oscar Chung) Another challenge to the species’ survival has been street dogs. Pangolins are easy targets because they move slowly, a concern that has grown after the culling of stray dogs was banned in 2017. According to Taipei Zoo, more than half of the pangolins treated at its rescue center suffered bite wounds from feral dogs. Conservation groups have responded with renewed outreach, habitat monitoring and public education to protect wild pangolins while promoting humane care for stray animals. Thanks to this sustained work, Taiwan’s pangolin population has rebounded and was estimated at around 15,000 in 2017, up from 10,000 in 2004. Globally, there are four surviving pangolin species in Africa and four in Asia. The Formosan pangolin, a subspecies of the Chinese pangolin, was among the first animals listed under the Act on Wildlife Conservation and appears in the Ministry of Agriculture’s (MOA) 2024 Red List of nationally threatened terrestrial mammals. Likewise, all eight pangolin species worldwide are now classified as threatened by the International Union for Conservation of Nature (IUCN), placing Taiwan’s conservation work firmly in line with global priorities. Kaohsiung resident Chen Tai-chu holds a pangolin about to be sent to National Pingtung University of Science and Technology for a health check-up. (Photo by Oscar Chung) Wild Learning With legal protection in place and ecological awareness steadily rising, researchers and conservationists have launched a series of government-supported projects to create a safer environment for pangolins. Among them is NPUST assistant professor Sun Ching-min, a pioneer in pangolin field research. Beginning in 2010 Sun spent eight years living in the Luanshan Indigenous community in Taitung County to observe pangolins in their natural habitat. His work produced one of the country’s most detailed databases on the species, documenting every stage of their life cycle. “Previously, there was very little information about pangolins living in the wild in Taiwan,” Sun said. “Only with sufficient data can you do conservation well, whether in the field or in managed environments.” Today Sun leads a 12-member research team at NPUST’s Institute of Wildlife Conservation, exploring Topics ranging from pangolin habitats to the animal’s life cycle and its role in the broader ecosystem. He also collects scales from pangolins found deceased around the country and tests them for traces of agricultural chemicals. The results help authorities refine regulations to ensure safer habitats for wildlife. Community engagement is another part of his mission. Shortly after the founding of KCMNHA, Sun began partnering with the organization, training Matoushan locals in field research and establishing a system for sending ill or injured pangolins to NPUST’s Pingtung Rescue Center for Wildlife, which he oversees. With the partnership now well established, Sun hopes to collaborate with more communities that host pangolin populations. 9a4b4809d35e7189552890a5bccf380bad3886fc: More than two decades have elapsed since Taiwan’s Gender Equity Education Act (GEEA, Gender Equity Education Act) went into effect on June 23, 2004. Since that time, continual efforts to renegotiate the act’s scope and content have encapsulated broader trends in national gender politics. The history of the GEEA has been characterized by notable advances in education reform, alongside structural challenges hindering full implementation of its provisions. Currently, the GEEA establishes a framework for equal educational rights, anti-discrimination protections in schools, and curricular instruction on gender diversity, sex education, and LGBTQ+ identity. These latter topics have become a particular source of contention for the act’s opponents, stymieing progress toward substantive equality. As educational initiatives related to gender diversity and inclusion come under growing scrutiny worldwide, the limitations and successes of the GEEA can serve as a reference for future policy interventions within and beyond Taiwan. Dokument vyzýva Európsku úniu, aby prehĺbila spoluprácu s demokratickými partnermi, akými sú Taiwan, Japonsko a Južná Kórea; opakuje, že je dôležité zachovať mier a stabilitu v Taiwanskom prielive; a stavia sa proti akýmkoľvek krokom, ktoré jednostranne menia status quo silou alebo nátlakom. Minister Lin vyjadruje svoje úprimné uznanie Európskemu parlamentu za to, že naďalej podniká konkrétne kroky na podporu Taiwanu. V odporúčaní sa uvádza, že Taiwan je dôveryhodným a kľúčovým demokratickým partnerom Európskej únie vo východnej Ázii a že mier a stabilita v Taiwanskom prielive a Juhočínskom mori sú pre Európsku úniu významným strategickým záujmom, ako aj životne dôležité pre globálnu bezpečnosť a prosperitu. Odporúča Európskej únii, aby posilnila spoluprácu s podobne zmýšľajúcimi partnermi vrátane Taiwanu, Japonska, Južnej Kórey a krajín ASEAN. Vychádzajúc z existujúcich mechanizmov, ako je dialóg o obchode a investíciách, odporúča, aby Európska únia a Taiwan vytvorili komplexný a štruktúrovaný rámec spolupráce. Text zároveň podporuje zmysluplnú účasť Taiwanu v medzinárodných organizáciách a technických fórach, vyzýva na dodržiavanie slobody plavby a preletov v Juhočínskom mori a Taiwanskom prielive a nabáda členov Európskeho parlamentu, aby posilnili parlamentnú diplomaciu taiwanským legislatívnym jüanom. Odporúčanie opäť zdôrazňuje dôležitosť, ktorú Európsky parlament pripisuje Taiwanu a mieru a stabilite naprieč úžinou. Po rezolúcii o obchodných a investičných vzťahoch medzi EÚ a Taiwanom z roku 2023, rezolúcii z roku 2024 o nesprávnom výklade rezolúcie Valného zhromaždenia OSN č. 2758 zo strany Čínskej ľudovej republiky a jej neustálych vojenských provokáciách okolo Taiwanu a po výročných správach o vykonávaní spoločnej zahraničnej a bezpečnostnej politiky EÚ za rok 2025 ide tiež o ďalšie podstatné vyjadrenie neochvejnej podpory Taiwanu. Taiwan bude pokračovať v posilňovaní spolupráce s Európskou úniou a podobne zmýšľajúcimi partnermi s cieľom spoločne chrániť mier a stabilitu v Taiwanskom prielive a Indo-pacifickom regióne, spoločne brániť medzinárodný poriadok založený na pravidlách a aktívne prispievať ku globálnemu mieru, bezpečnosti a prosperite. Súvisiaci odkaz: Odporúčanie o meniacej sa geopolitickej situácii vo východnej Ázii a potrebe užšej spolupráce s podobne zmýšľajúcimi partnermi v regióne.

4a49eea2d0dc62c2849bf8e7ad69d2ad38353c09: Prezident Lai Ching-te poukázal na dôležitosť výmeny medzi mestami pre pokračujúci rozvoj partnerstva Taiwanu s Japonskom v poznámkach, ktoré privítali delegáciu vedenú starostom Tetsuo Setaka z mesta Nikko, prefektúra Tochigi, 8. júla v prezidentskej kancelárii v meste Taipei. Prezident poznamenal, že Taiwan a Japonsko sú hlavnými partnermi, ktorí spoločne riešia problémy, a dodal, že po ničivom zemetrasení vo východnom Japonsku v roku 2011 viedol delegáciu do Nikko ako starosta mesta Tainan na podporu miestneho cestovného ruchu. Lai tiež uznala Nikkove fundraisingové kampane v Tainan a Hualien County po tom, čo regióny zažili ničivé zemetrasenia v roku 2016 a 2024. Obe krajiny okrem technológie, obchodu a cestovného ruchu aktívne spolupracujú aj v kultúrnych a ekonomických záležitostiach, povedal Lai. Dodal, že v roku 2025 objem bilaterálneho obchodu presiahol 84,8 miliardy USD, čo je o 17,36 % viac ako v predchádzajúcom roku, pričom počet recipročných návštev prekročil 8,21 milióna, čím sa dosiahol rekordný nárast. Podľa PO Setaka odpovedal, že predchádzajúci deň vzal dobrovoľníkov a zástupcov cestovných kancelárií Nikko do Tainanu z obavy o obnovu mesta po zemetraseniach a tajfúnoch v minulom roku. PO uviedol, že vzal na vedomie 17-ročné puto, ktoré si tieto dve mestá vybudovali podporou vzájomného cestovného ruchu, a teší sa na ďalšie prehĺbenie väzieb na spoločné napredovanie výmen v oblasti kultúry, hospodárstva a športu. 3c347f9ab74d67059ab82c6596ae621147faeadd: President Lai Ching-te met with a delegation led by Guatemalan Congress President Luis Alberto Contreras Colíndres at the Presidential Office July 8 in Taipei City and anticipated enhanced partnership between the allies to promote mutual prosperity and progress. Lai said Taiwan-Guatemala relations have continued positive forward momentum over recent years, especially in the areas of medical care, industrial development and trade. In particular, Lai said he and President Bernardo Aréval concluded a letter of intent to expand semiconductor cooperation during the latter’s visit in June last year. In addition to semiconductor cooperation, Lai said the two allies have also expanded bilateral trade, as evidenced by the US$130 million in annual exports from Guatemala to Taiwan for two years in a row, making it the leading supplier of cane sugar and fourth largest supplier of coffee to Taiwan. The president thanked Contreras for signing a resolution calling for Taiwan’s inclusion of the World Health Organization, as well as for strong congressional support for Taiwan’s participation in international bodies. The government encourages domestic firms to enjoy Guatemala’s many strategic strengths as they seek to expand a presence in American markets. In response, Contreras said Guatemala has always been a loyal friend to Taiwan and anticipated an ever-more beneficial long term bond. He praised Taiwan as an inspiring example in terms of social development, technological innovation and economic growth. On behalf of Guatemala, Contreras thanked the government of Taiwan for its assistance, especially in modernizing the Congress through various cooperative projects. He also reiterated congressional support for expanding partnership with Taiwan, and commended the country’s success in economic, social and democratic development. 25460927afd8e33142678feb2905186f569338c1: Prezident Lai Ching-te prijal delegáciu zloženú z členov U.S. National Endowment for Democracy a jej kľúčových partnerov v prezidentskej kancelárii 7. júla v meste Taipei. Podľa PO vedie skupinu prezident a generálny riaditeľ NED Damon Wilson, ktorý je na Taiwane piatykrát od roku 2022, keď ho navštívil ako prvú zastávku svojho prvého ázijského turné ako šéf mimovládnej organizácie so sídlom vo Washingtone D.C. Lai povedal, že rok 2026 je 250. výročím založenia USA a 30. výročím prvých priamych prezidentských volieb na Taiwane. Na opačných stranách Tichého oceánu ich spájajú spoločné hodnoty slobody a demokracie a spolupracujú pri riešení globálnych výziev, dodal. Prezident uviedol, že vojenské aktivity Číny a vpády do šedej zóny v Taiwanskom prielive a proti susedným krajinám majú vážny vplyv na regionálny mier a stabilitu, zatiaľ čo jej rozsiahle nadnárodné represie a dohľad znepokojujú medzinárodné spoločenstvo. Taiwan neustále posilňuje svoje schopnosti sebaobrany a zvyšuje odolnosť miestnej ekonomiky, technológií a energetiky, uviedol prezident. Spolupracuje tiež s USA a ďalšími demokratickými partnermi, povedal Lai a teší sa na zdieľanie skúseností s delegátmi NED, aby mohli lepšie reagovať na výzvy rozširujúceho sa autoritárstva. V reakcii na to Wilson ocenil Taiwan ako jeden z najväčších demokratických úspechov na svete a dodal, že jeho ľudia vybudovali pulzujúcu demokraciu, konkurenčné voľby a dynamickú občiansku spoločnosť. NED je hrdý na to, že tento týždeň môže na Taiwane privítať delegátov z viac ako 70 krajín na summite, aby sa podelili o skúsenosti z Taiwanu s obhajcami demokracie a posilnili partnerstvá na podporu slobody, dodal. c34343e308292350f1f9d44a5f9355cd4bc45ebe: Prezident Lai Ching-te prijal delegáciu vedenú americkou senátorkou Tammy Duckworth v prezidentskej kancelárii v meste Taipei. Členmi delegácie boli Michael Frerichs, štátny pokladník štátu Illinois, a Paul Faraci, senátor štátu Illinois, uviedol PO. Lai poznamenal, že Taiwan a USA sú dôležitými ekonomickými a strategickými partnermi a určili si spoluprácu v sektore bezpilotných lietadiel s cieľom uľahčiť recipročný hospodársky a obranný rozvoj, posilniť demokratickú a vedeckú odolnosť a prispieť k mieru a prosperite. Lai ďalej poďakoval Duckworthovi za vedenie medzistraníckeho senátneho uznesenia na pripomenutie si 30. výročia priamych prezidentských volieb na Taiwane v marci tohto roku. Uviedol, že v priebehu rokov Duckworthová navrhla niekoľko taiwanských priateľských rezolúcií a citoval jej obhajobu darovania vakcín Taiwanu. Pokiaľ ide o vzťah cez úžinu, Lai povedal, že Taiwan sa zaviazal k posilneniu schopností sebaobrany, o čom svedčí súčasný rozpočet na obranu, ktorý predstavuje viac ako 3 percentá hrubého domáceho produktu a predpokladá sa, že do roku 2030 dosiahne 5 percent. Lai poďakoval Duckworthovi, vojenskému veteránovi, za uľahčenie spolupráce medzi Taiwanom a USA. spolupráca v priemysle bezpilotných lietadiel. Očakával, že Taiwan bude v budúcnosti zohrávať úlohu ázijského priemyselného centra v tejto oblasti s podporou Kongresu, vlády a Senátu USA. Duckworth uviedol, že podpora Kongresu USA pre Taiwan zahŕňa ekonomiku, humanitárnu pomoc a bezpečnostnú spoluprácu. Bezpečnosť Taiwanu je úzko spätá s bezpečnosťou USA, keďže konflikt v Taiwanskom prielive by mohol mať za následok finančný globálny dopad okolo 10 biliónov USD, dodala. Taiwan sa stal štvrtým najväčším obchodným partnerom pre USA v roku 2025 a USA sa stali najväčším obchodným partnerom Taiwanu v prvom štvrťroku tohto roka. Vláda bude naďalej podporovať vzájomné investície a obchodnú výmenu. (POC-E) Napíšte na Taiwan ešte dnes na ttonline@mofa.gov.tw
